input: Coordinate meal train for a friend post-surgery

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many days or weeks of meals are needed shapes the entire size and structure of the meal train — a 1-week recovery differs vastly from a 6-week one.
The pool of potential meal contributors (close friends only, extended community, neighborhood, religious group, etc.) determines how to reach out and how many slots can realistically be filled.
Dietary restrictions, allergies, or food preferences of the recovering friend are hard limits that every contributor must know before cooking.
Whether to use an existing platform (MealTrain.com, SignUpGenius, group chat) or coordinate manually determines the immediate first step and ongoing communication flow.
The surgery date and when the friend returns home sets the start date and urgency of the planning — setup needs to happen before meals are needed.
The friend's preferences around drop-off (contactless vs. visit, time of day, portion sizes, homemade vs. restaurant) affect the instructions given to contributors.
Understanding what the user considers a fully covered meal train — e.g., every dinner covered, or breakfast and dinner, or full days — defines when the task is actually done.

gold.taskTitle: Coordinate meal train for post-surgery friend
gold.taskDescription: Organize a rotating schedule of meals delivered by friends, family, or community members to support a friend recovering from surgery.

questions.title: How many weeks of meals does your friend need?
questions.description: Determine the total duration of the meal train to know how many delivery slots need to be filled.

questions.title: Who is the contributor pool — friends, family, community group?
questions.description: Identify the group of people who will be invited to sign up so outreach can be planned appropriately.

questions.title: Does your friend have any dietary restrictions or allergies?
questions.description: Capture hard food limits that must be communicated to every contributor before they cook or order.

questions.title: Which tool will you use to manage sign-ups?
questions.description: Decide whether to use a dedicated platform like MealTrain.com or SignUpGenius, or coordinate via group chat or spreadsheet.

questions.title: When does your friend come home from the hospital?
questions.description: Establish the start date so the meal train can be set up and communicated to contributors before the first delivery is needed.

questions.title: What are your friend's drop-off preferences — time, contact, portions?
questions.description: Clarify whether the friend wants contactless drop-offs, specific delivery windows, or other personal preferences to include in contributor instructions.

questions.title: Which meals per day count as fully covered to you?
questions.description: Define what a successfully completed meal train looks like — dinners only, two meals a day, or full-day coverage — so there is a clear finish line.
